key_insight: Quantum simulation cost is strongly family-dependent, and adding family-aware residual corrections lets a model predict both the needed approximation threshold and runtime from an OpenQASM circuit description.
engineering_relevance: This can replace slow trial-and-error tuning for tensor-network simulators, helping engineers choose simulation settings in milliseconds instead of running expensive test simulations.
method: Shared neural backbone on circuit + execution-context features
Pretrained family classifier (97.5% accuracy) plus algorithm fingerprint heuristics
Family-specific residual heads to adjust threshold and runtime predictions
evidence_signal: Across circuits from 7 to 130 qubits in 10 algorithm families, the method reached 79.5% exact threshold accuracy, 91.2% within one rung, and runtime prediction correlation of R² = 0.82 with about 50 ms inference.
watch_item: Performance may depend on accurate family classification and on how well the training data covers new circuit families or unusual entanglement patterns.
paper_title: Family-Aware Residual Architecture for Predicting Quantum Circuit Simulation Performance
